solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leisurely plebeian follows society

indicators.note: follows places the word for plebeian after the letter for society

parts.note: plebeian means of humble rank, lowly

explanation.surface: A relaxed commoner trailing along behind high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a leisurely pace means doing it without haste, unhurriedly.

clue.text: Clean tart seen outside clubs

indicators.note: seen outside places the word for tart around the clubs letter

parts.note: tart and sour both describe a sharp taste
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A cleaner tart spotted leaving a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' reads as a person, but it is the adjective for sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a surface hard with something abrasive is a way of cleaning it.

clue.text: Like smells left in old assembly plant

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the combination of old and factory

parts.note: a factory is a plant where goods are assembled

explanation.surface: The odours left lingering in a disused car plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The olfactory sense is the sense of smell, so this adjective means relating to scents.

clue.text: Song was lacking in volume

indicators.note: lacking says the volume letter is missing from the word for was

parts.note: to have lived is to have existed, so was can mean lived

explanation.surface: A song that was too quiet to hear properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness, but it is the letter V.
explanation.definitionFit: This German word names an art song, as composed by Schubert or Schumann.

clue.text: Spotted quick kiss in sledge

indicators.note: in places the quick kiss inside the word for sledge

parts.note: a sled is another word for a sledge
a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: Someone was seen stealing a quick kiss on a sledge ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as 'seen', but it is the definition in its sense of marked with dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a surface covered with small dots or flecks of colour.

clue.text: Kilometres covered in walking holiday activity

indicators.note: covered in places the kilometre letter inside the walking word

parts.note: pacing is walking with steady steps
K is short for kilometres

explanation.surface: Kilometres clocked on a hiking holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling a suitcase is a task done before going away on a trip.

clue.text: Who'll not be shut up in rabbit hutch?

definitions.note: a person who refuses to stop talking

parts.note: in British slang to rabbit on is to talk at length, to chatter
a hutch is a box or cage for keeping rabbits

explanation.surface: A rabbit that will not stay locked in its hutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the animal, but in British slang it means to talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks incessantly will never be silenced, the sense of shut up as be quiet.

clue.text: Large country where I lost girl

indicators.note: lost says the letter I goes missing from the country

parts.note: India is a large country

explanation.surface: A girl lost somewhere in a vast country.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is a common female first name, so it stands for a particular girl.

clue.text: Half deny being selfish, grabbing a chance to receive an award

indicators.note: Half takes the front two of the four letters of deny
grabbing means the selfish word takes hold of the letter a inside it

parts.note: greedy describes someone selfish, wanting more

explanation.surface: A grasping person grabs at any opportunity for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the occasion at a university when students go up to be awarded their qualifications.

clue.text: Small carrier of canvas for drawing

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, carrying canvas sails

explanation.surface: A little bag for carrying painting canvases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' suggests an artist, but here it is sailcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, quick drawing is a preliminary study made before a fuller picture.

clue.text: Where mountaineer comes when it's not so busy

definitions.meaning: a climber coming down from the summit comes off the top of the mountain
describes travel or calls at quieter, cheaper times of day

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a descent from a summit; as one word it means outside the busiest hours.

clue.text: Casually going to Roman Catholic returning home in Ireland once

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the whole string from the end back to the start

parts.note: gonna is the casual spoken form of going to

explanation.surface: Someone drifting back to the Catholic faith in a relaxed way.
explanation.definitionFit: A crannog was an ancient lake dwelling built on an artificial island, found in Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Stack of building blocks uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered says the word loses its outside letters, its covering

parts.note: bricks are the blocks used in building

explanation.surface: A pile of toy blocks left with the lid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips B and S from BRICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay, straw or corn, built in a field.

clue.text: Tapestries reworked in gradual removal of threads

indicators.note: reworked suggests the letters of the word are being made over into a new order

explanation.surface: Old tapestries being unpicked and remade, thread by thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'threads' looks like textile yarn, matching the tapestries, but it is slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads is slang for clothes, and a performer peeling them off slowly is doing a burlesque undressing act.

clue.text: Doubt returning editor will fill opening

indicators.note: will fill puts the reversed editor letters inside the opening

parts.note: an incision is a cut that opens something

indicators.note: returning says the editor letters run backwards

explanation.surface: An uncertain editor comes back to plug a vacancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to make up one's mind is a state of uncertainty.

clue.text: Marmot moved with much effort, having initially run back

parts.note: ground, past tense of grind, as in a lorry that ground up the hill

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word having
back means the word for run is read in reverse

parts.note: go can mean run, as of a machine or a race

explanation.surface: A marmot struggling along and then scurrying back.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodchuck of North America is a species of marmot, a large burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Physically agile as McGinty's dancing

indicators.note: dancing means the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: As nimble as a man named McGinty when he dances.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of McGinty's is 'is', a link before 'dancing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lithe and athletic moves like a trained gymnast.

clue.text: Was angry with newspaper and its head

parts.note: rag is a dismissive word for a newspaper
the editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A reader fumed at a paper and at the person running it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to be furious, so a past-tense form fits a past-tense phrase for being cross.

clue.text: Girl extremely loving and very attractive

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme, outermost letters of the word girl

parts.note: amorous means loving, inclined to romance

explanation.surface: A girl who is deeply affectionate and very good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring charm, so someone with it is highly appealing.

clue.text: For all one knows millions certainly exist

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million or millions
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, certainly
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Millions of things surely exist out there, as far as anyone can say.
explanation.definitionFit: Both express uncertainty: something possibly so, without proof either way.

clue.text: General sent out army scout

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters are dispatched and scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A commanding officer dispatches a reconnaissance soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank to match army and scout, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and general both describe what is common practice or widely followed.

clue.text: Tropical pest excavator found under church, losing days

indicators.note: under places the excavator word below the church letters in this down clue
losing means the day letter is dropped from the excavator

parts.note: a digger is a mechanical excavator

explanation.surface: A digger turns up below a church, out of action for days.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tiny mite larva of warm regions whose bite causes intense itching.

clue.text: Posed around Europe for artist

indicators.note: around puts the word for posed about the Europe letters

parts.note: a model sat for a portrait, posed

explanation.surface: A model posed all over Europe for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Seurat was the French painter who pioneered pointillism.

clue.text: Encouraging son to leave a suspect

indicators.note: to leave says the letter for son goes away from the phrase

parts.note: a suspect thing is suspicious, open to doubt
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent hoping the boy will steer clear of a dubious character.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspicious start is a promising one, favourable and full of hope.

clue.text: Stole line written by playwright

indicators.note: written by places the line letter beside the dramatist's name

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist's line stolen by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a wide scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders.

clue.text: Section of filled pizza with no calories

indicators.note: with no tells us to remove the calorie letters from the pizza

parts.note: a calzone is a folded pizza with filling inside
cal is the abbreviation for calories

explanation.surface: A slice of stuffed pizza that is somehow free of calories.
explanation.definitionFit: An area or region set apart, such as a time or parking district, is a distinct part of a larger whole.

clue.text: Get rid of European judge over English court

indicators.note: over places the European judge above the English court in a down entry

explanation.surface: A European judge throws out a case heard by an English court.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out or expel something is to remove it forcibly.

clue.text: Hat perched on back of the head

indicators.note: perched on sets the hat above the following letter in this down entry

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat

indicators.note: back of takes the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A hat sitting on the back of someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like part of the body, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland or promontory jutting into the sea, such as Cape Horn.

clue.text: Finding time and doing competitive sport

parts.note: racing is a competitive sport, on foot, horseback or in cars

explanation.surface: Someone discovers time to take part in races.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing a missing person or item means tracking it down and locating it.

clue.text: A Yankee sausage, not Yankee shellfish

indicators.note: not says the Y letter is taken away from the sausage word

parts.note: baloney is the American spelling of bologna sausage
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American sausage served with no Yankee in it but shellfish instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Clay urn I adapted for cooking

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A potter alters a clay pot to use in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes anything relating to the kitchen or the preparing of food.

clue.text: Organ piece appearing in Carver setting

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Music for the organ is played at a church carving ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A verset is a short piece for organ, often replacing a verse of a sung text in a service.
